theme: The lampstand; the flying scroll; the Branch crowned
readingInstruction: Read Zechariah 4:1-6:15. You will read the remaining four visions: the lampstand and olive trees, the flying scroll, the woman in a basket, and the four chariots. The chapter ends with a crowning ceremony for Joshua. Read 4:6 and 6:12-13 carefully.
settingTheScene: The visions continue. The fifth vision shows a golden lampstand fed by two olive trees, and it is meant to encourage Zerubbabel, the governor who is leading the temple’s rebuilding. The next three visions deal with sin, and the eighth shows God’s judgment on the nations. The section ends with a symbolic act: the crowning of the high priest Joshua, who stands as a picture of the Messiah.
observation: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of hosts” (4:6).
“Who has despised the day of small things? For these seven shall rejoice, when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel” (4:10).
“These are the two anointed ones who stand by the Lord of the whole earth” (4:14).
“This is the curse that goes out over the face of the whole land” (5:3).
“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also complete it” (4:9).
“Take from the exiles… silver and gold, and make a crown” (6:10-11).
“Behold, the man whose name is the Branch: for he shall branch out from his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD” (6:12).
“And he shall bear royal honor, and shall sit and rule on his throne. And there shall be a priest on his throne” (6:13).
interpretation:
The lampstand vision is among the best known. Zechariah sees a golden lampstand with seven lamps, fed with oil from two olive trees through pipes, with no human hand pouring. The meaning is given in a single sentence: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.” Zerubbabel faces a mountain of difficulty, and he is told that the work will be done by the Spirit of God, not by human strength. The oil is the Spirit, the light is the witness of God’s people, and the supply is limitless. “Who has despised the day of small things?” The small beginning would be finished.

The next three visions are about sin. The flying scroll, thirty feet by fifteen, goes out over the land with a curse on thieves and those who swear falsely. The woman in the basket, “Wickedness,” is carried away to Babylon. God is not just rebuilding a building. He is removing evil from the land. This answers the problem that Ezra and Nehemiah faced: how could the community stay faithful? God would purge it.

The eighth vision of the four chariots goes out to the four winds, and the one going north has “set my Spirit at rest in the north country.” God’s judgment on Babylon is complete.

Then the symbolic act: Zechariah is told to make a crown and set it on the head of Joshua the high priest, and say, “Behold, the man whose name is the Branch.” Joshua is not the Branch himself; he is a sign. The Branch will build the temple, sit and rule on his throne, “and there shall be a priest on his throne.” In Israel, kings and priests were separate. But the Messiah would hold both offices. “The counsel of peace shall be between them both.” This is a clear promise of a priest-king, who is Jesus. And “those who are far off shall come and help to build the temple of the LORD.” The Gentiles will join.
connection: Hebrews 7:1-3 and Psalm 110:4 describe a priest-king in the order of Melchizedek. Hebrews 4:14-16 names Jesus our great high priest. Luke 1:78 calls Jesus the “sunrise” or “Branch.” Revelation 11:4 uses the two olive trees. Galatians 5:16-25 teaches walking by the Spirit. Acts 1:8: “You will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.” Ephesians 2:19-22 shows Gentiles built into the temple.
application:
Where are you trying “by might and by power”? Pray, “Not by my strength, but by your Spirit.”

Don’t despise a small beginning. Ask God to finish what he started.

Thank Jesus that he is both king and priest, and has done what Joshua only pictured.
prayerPrompts: Tell God that it is not by might or power but by his Spirit.
Ask him not to let you despise the day of small things.
Ask him to remove wickedness from your life.
